what: Actionable synthesis of the 63-paper full-text dossier and the reproduced-method record (2026-10-21 continuous-traversal directive). Every non-pending idea below is tied to a fresh measurement artifact; every compared method has both an appreciation and an evidence-backed critique in deep_read.json.

coverage.scope_note: Full texts were read from exp/literature/papers/*.txt; the dossier covers CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/NeurIPS/AAAI/ICML and arXiv, with 40 RIS/same-class papers and 21 RIS/adjacent, plus 17 successful repo runs, including 10 full-split method runs (LAVT and EVF-SAM added as exact full-val reproductions) (full val where the pipeline is released, explicit small batteries otherwise).

ideas.idea: Use the released S+S reverse-blur visual prompt as an independent zero-shot selection rule on the shared SAM pool.
ideas.test: Full official val with exp188_splus_repro.py; released vp_and_max_sim_clip_choice, reverse_blur, CLIP ViT-B/32, SAM ViT-H pps 8 pool; wrong-instance share computed under the same threshold definition as the diagnosis.
ideas.measured: 29.46/35.35/38.92 mIoU, wrong-instance shares 95.4/94.7/93.2% on RefCOCO/+/g; published stage-1 pool is GroundingDINO+SAM, so its level is cross-harness but the gap composition replicates.
ideas.decision: Kept as a third released selection pipeline in the diagnosis table; not promoted as a selector because its level is below the shipped method.

ideas.idea: Rectangle visual prompts are a better selection prompt than reverse blur.
ideas.test: Same released S+S rule, mask replaced by a red bounding rectangle at the proposal box, full official val (exp188 --method rectangle).
ideas.measured: 8.91/10.20/10.57 mIoU with wrong-instance shares 96.7/96.5/95.3%; a 20-28 point drop from reverse blur on every dataset.
ideas.decision: The rectangle variant is retained only as a labelled released-prompt sensitivity row with comparable:false; the paper states the negative result explicitly.

ideas.idea: Released Global-Local token masking can serve as an external selector on a shared pool and as a check on the selection diagnosis.
ideas.test: Faithful port of the released CLIPViTFM masking head (masking_block=9, last_layer=11) with CLIP ViT-B/32 on the SAM ViT-H pool, full official val.
ideas.measured: 32.95/36.31/41.62 mIoU, wrong-instance shares 95.1/94.2/92.5%; its own FreeSOLO pool is unobtainable, but the independent 2026 comparison in earlygrounding2026 reports 33.12/35.29/40.08 for the ViT-B variant, within 0.2-1.6 mIoU of our reproduction.
ideas.decision: Kept as an independent pipeline and as an external validity check; the paper adds the cross-reference and still labels the published 31.83/34.97/40.66 as published, not pooled with our numbers.

ideas.idea: MaskCLIP's dense value map can be used as a training-free component pool; if the pool is the bottleneck, its oracle cap should be low.
ideas.test: Released MaskCLIP dense map with the final ln_post before proj, own component pool at fixed 50/70/90th percentile thresholds, top-12 by mean value, full official val; plus the same dense map on the shared SAM pool as a control.
ideas.measured: Own-pool 8.21/10.55/14.30 mIoU with oracle caps 25.2/28.1/31.8 and wrong-instance shares only 24.3/27.3/31.6%; on the SAM pool 8.15/9.83/11.57 mIoU with wrong-instance shares 96.7/96.3/95.2%.
ideas.decision: Kept as the pool-limited boundary case. The paper now also cites the 2026 earlygrounding2026 table, which reports a SAM-proposal MaskCLIP at 25.62/27.49/30.13 mIoU, as evidence that our row is an adaptation of the dense-map component pool, not MaskCLIP's strongest released route.

ideas.idea: GEM self-self attention coherence alone can replace the released semantic selector.
ideas.test: Full official val re-analysis of the stored per-proposal GEM coherence scores (exp189_gem_selector.py): argmax coherence versus the released final pick and argmax semantic score, same pool and candidate set.
ideas.measured: GEM-only 44.81/32.81/42.20 mIoU versus released 44.82/40.23/50.08 and argmax-semantic 35.18/38.79/46.48 on RefCOCO/+/g. GEM-only matches the released selector on RefCOCO (delta 0.01) but loses 7.4 and 7.9 mIoU on RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg.
ideas.decision: Adopted as a measured ablation (full official val, exp189_gem_selector.py) and rejected as a method replacement: coherence-only matches the released selector on RefCOCO but loses 7.4-7.9 mIoU on RefCOCO+/g. The shipped method is unchanged.

ideas.idea: A set-valued selector is needed for gRefCOCO multi-target references; a single-box rule cannot represent two targets.
ideas.test: Shipped gRefCOCO selector on the full official val (per-sentence protocol, ref_id-keyed terms corrected) with the term-alignment fix; cIoU/gIoU/N-acc/T-acc under the official evaluator.
ideas.measured: 47.5854 cIoU / 73.7800 gIoU, N_acc 85.66, T_acc 88.71 on 14,229 val rows; corrects the earlier 50.99/51.32 record that used ref_id-keyed terms misaligned on 84.7% of targeted multi-sentence rows.
ideas.decision: Kept and shipped; best_published remains SELF1E-8B 44.4 cIoU and PSALM 43.3 gIoU, both same-class published numbers.

ideas.idea: A VLM can select among numbered candidate overlays (Set-of-Mark) and replace the region-text selector.
ideas.test: Top-8 SAM candidates tinted and numbered; GLM-4.1V asked for the index on 200 cached RefCOCO val rows; parsed answers used, unparsed answers fall back to the released pick.
ideas.measured: Set-of-Mark selection reaches 39.13 mIoU versus the released pick on the same rows and falls below the shipped selector; the VLM's index answer is not reliable enough to replace the score.
ideas.decision: Retained as a falsification probe; no VLM-in-the-loop selection is shipped. This is consistent with the literature's MLLM selectors being trained (ResAgent, DSS), not off-the-shelf.

ideas.idea: A small learned localization prior fitted on a train carve-out can improve gRefCOCO part acceptance without touching val.
ideas.test: HistGradientBoosting part-acceptance prior over the existing 12-dim per-part features, trained on 70% of gRefCOCO train with 30% held out; threshold selected on the held-out carve-out; official val evaluated once.
ideas.measured: The prior fixed the measured train-to-val part-quality shift (part IoU 0.413 train vs 0.355 val) and was measured under the light-supervision allowance, but after the per-sentence term-alignment correction its promoted recipe measures 49.40/74.26 cIoU/gIoU and its part pool is detector-derived, so it is not shipped under the DINO-free requirement. It remains a labelled ablation.
ideas.decision: Rejected for the shipped gRefCOCO rule: the detector-free VLM-box SAM rule is shipped instead, and the acceptance prior is kept only in the detector-bearing ablation and appendix provenance record. The earlier 52.71/75.08 promotion is withdrawn as a term-alignment artifact.

ideas.idea: Declare and isolate the trained selector head rather than pretending the full pipeline is training-free.
ideas.test: Drop-one attribution on full val: remove the box prior, remove the restriction, and rebuild the head from our own mechanisms (exp/out_final/component_provenance.json).
ideas.measured: The shipped head reaches 70.57/66.35/65.51 mIoU; given the restriction, the box is worth +25.21/+26.82/+17.61 mIoU, while the restriction is roughly neutral given the box. The training-free reference rule stays at 68.53/64.67/65.12.
ideas.decision: The paper states the trained component and its provenance explicitly; the training-free rule is kept as the reference arm. This is the only trained component in the RefCOCO-family pipeline.

ideas.idea: Mid-layer spatial maps are a better grounding signal than final-layer embeddings for spatial expressions.
ideas.test: Not yet run: extract a mid-layer CLIP spatial map for the RefCOCO val proposals and add it as a re-ranking term for parsed spatial expressions, with the same gate and no val tuning.
ideas.decision: Candidate for the next cycle; the paper's reported 1-7 mIoU gain is on a different selector and does not establish that it repairs wrong-instance selection rather than boundaries.

ideas.idea: Attribute prompting with an LLM over SAM proposals improves implicit and part-level references.
ideas.test: Not yet run at full scale: generate shape/colour/location attributes for proposals and re-rank; the cost is one LLM call per expression/proposal set.
ideas.decision: The published method is training-free but uses a large LLM and evaluates cIoU, not mIoU; its 68.5 cIoU on RefCOCO val is not directly comparable to our 70.57 mIoU. A cost-controlled test on the held-out carve-out is needed before adoption.

ideas.idea: Region-consistent inference over frozen CLIP tokens (region graph, cross-window context, reference memory) can improve the feature path.
ideas.test: Not yet run: apply a region-consistent affinity smoothing to the per-proposal G2L features and re-evaluate the selector on the held-out carve-out.
ideas.decision: Strong training-free OVSS gains (+7.6 mIoU) but no referring expressions and no instance selection; it is a feature-path repair whose effect on our wrong-instance mass is unknown.

ideas.idea: Use a diffusion or DiT attention readout as a zero-shot RIS prior.
ideas.test: Not run: the 9-12B generative backbones and multi-step diffusion readouts are outside our compute budget and deployment class.
ideas.decision: The reported 57.56 mIoU (Step1X-Edit) is below our shipped 70.57 on RefCOCO val, and the cost is orders of magnitude higher; it is a reference point, not a candidate method.

ideas.idea: Replace the frozen CLIP selection path with a fine-grained region-text backbone (FG-CLIP) inside a training-free search.
ideas.test: RefChess released MCTS pipeline with the FG-CLIP base backbone on a 120-expression sample (exp/literature/repos/refchess, 16 simulations, GEM heatmap).
ideas.decision: The 120-sample run is a sample, not a full pipeline; the dense FG-CLIP path previously hit OOM/shape mismatches. The result is recorded as an ongoing run, not a promoted selection rule.

ideas.idea: Feed output-based patch correspondences back into CLIP attention (plug-in feedback) to repair frozen features.
ideas.test: Not yet run: requires modifying the CLIP visual forward pass and re-extracting proposal features; the paper reports +7.9 mIoU on MaskCLIP ViT-B/16.
ideas.decision: Promising feature-path repair, but it does not select instances and its OVSS benchmarks have fixed vocabularies; a held-out test is needed before any paper claim.

ideas.idea: Restore spatial priors with intermediate-layer QQ attention and guided upsampling (SatOV).
ideas.test: Not yet run: port ResQQ to the CLIP ViT-B/32 feature path and measure on the held-out carve-out.
ideas.decision: Remote-sensing-specific and class-level; the transfer to referring expressions is speculative, and its +5.6 mIoU SatUp gain may mostly repair boundaries rather than wrong instances.

ideas.idea: Use expression rewriting / target prompts to make spatial and attribute language explicit before scoring.
ideas.test: Not yet run as a standalone arm: our shipped parsed-spatial operator is the training-free analogue, and its gain is measured only on the parsed subset (main_refcoco.json).
ideas.decision: A full-expression rewrite arm without the parsed-vocabulary restriction is the natural next test; the published target-prompt result is trained and reports relative gains only.

gaps.gap: No common cross-harness protocol: the same released HybridGL is 49.48/43.40/51.25 mIoU in their table and 44.82/40.23/50.08 in our reproduction, while MaskCLIP is 25.62/27.49/30.13 there and 8.21/10.55/14.30 in our dense-map adaptation. Zero-shot RIS tables do not report pool, feature path or evaluator consistently, so published rows cannot be pooled with reproduced rows.

Released zero-shot pipelines frequently omit the artifacts needed for full reproduction: the FreeSOLO R101 pool URL does not resolve, TAS requires a per-sentence BLIP-2 caption file it does not ship, Ref-Diff releases no segmenter checkpoint, and PSALM's detectron2 stack is not buildable in our environment. Evidence-backed blockers, not negative results.

gaps.paper: cmsa2019 through the 2026 RIS papers in the dossier
gaps.gap: Almost no paper reports a selection-level metric separate from mask IoU. Aggregate mIoU/cIoU hides whether the error is a wrong instance, an undersegmented correct instance or a boundary miss; our taxonomy is the exception and shows wrong-instance selection carries 94.0/94.2/91.8% of the recoverable mass for HybridGL.

Multi-target and no-target gRefCOCO remains far from solved in the training-free class: supervised ReLA reaches 62.91 cIoU / 63.98 gIoU, while our corrected training-free row is 47.59 cIoU / 73.78 gIoU. The gIoU parity does not transfer to cIoU, and N-acc is a separate axis where training helps.

The feature path imposes a ceiling that selection repair cannot cross: EVF-SAM's controlled comparison moves a CLIP-prompted SAM from 63.4 to 83.7 cIoU by changing only the text/fusion path. Our frozen CLIP selector is on the low side of that gap, and no training-free paper in the dossier closes it without a trained fusion or decoder.

The new zero-shot RIS frontier is moving to 9-12B generative backbones and trained MLLM decoders (57.56 mIoU on RefCOCO val for Step1X-Edit, 82.8 for Qwen3-VL-Seg). These are different deployment classes and different supervision classes; no paper provides a cost-controlled comparison against training-free selectors on the same pool.

Spatial-language handling is diagnosed but not connected to instance selection. Mid-layer probing, spatial-prior restoration and target prompts all report gains, but none reports whether the gain is on the parsed-spatial subset, whether the correct instance is selected, or whether the mask boundary improved.

adopted_this_cycle.idea: GEM coherence-only selection under the same pool and candidate set (gem2023), measured on all three full official val splits.
adopted_this_cycle.result: GEM-only reaches 44.81/32.81/42.20 mIoU versus the released 44.82/40.23/50.08 (RefCOCO/+/g). Coherence is sufficient on RefCOCO but not on RefCOCO+/g, so the released semantic-plus-coherence rule is retained.
adopted_this_cycle.paper_change: The diagnosis now cites the probe and the independent earlygrounding2026 cross-check; the method and the SOTA table are unchanged.

verdict: The literature supports the diagnosis in its conditional form and sharpens its boundaries. Selection is a first-class stage in independent work (S+S's explicit select step, DSS's semantic mask selection, RefChess's stability-aware search), and every released selector we could run on a common pool shows the same failure composition: wrong-instance selection carries 91.8-95.4% of the recoverable IoU when the pool contains the referent. At the same time, the dossier contains three honest limits. First, the feature path matters: EVF-SAM's controlled early-fusion comparison moves a CLIP-prompted SAM from 63.4 to 83.7 cIoU, and our frozen CLIP path sits on the low side of that gap. Second, coherence is not enough by itself: GEM-only selection matches the released HybridGL on RefCOCO (44.81 vs 44.82 mIoU) but loses 7.4-7.9 mIoU on RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg, so the semantic term is load-bearing exactly where attribute and compositional language dominate. Third, the field's published zero-shot numbers are not pool-, feature- or evaluator-matched: an independent 2026 table puts HybridGL 4.7 mIoU above our faithful released-code reproduction and MaskCLIP 17 mIoU above our dense-map adaptation, which is why the paper keeps published rows labelled as published and confines the GLOD-RIS reproduction to the appendix. Implications for our claims: (i) the RefCOCO-family SOTA claim rests on the shipped 70.57/66.35/65.51 versus the best same-class published 58.42/54.01/57.85 and is unchanged; (ii) the gRefCOCO claim rests on 47.59 cIoU / 73.78 gIoU versus SELF1E-8B 44.4 and PSALM 43.3 and is unchanged, with the supervised ReLA 62.91/63.98 kept as a labelled reference; (iii) we explicitly do not claim a universal selection law, and we add the MaskCLIP SAM-proposal caveat and the Global-Local independent cross-check to the diagnosis; (iv) the one measured idea adopted this cycle, GEM-only selection, is reported as a scoped ablation and does not alter the method. The training-free versus trained boundary is stated plainly: the RefCOCO-family learned selector is the declared trained component, and the training-free reference rule is reported separately.
